post.caption: Harry Winston named a diamond Portuguese. The Portuguese Diamond weighs about 127 carats. A legend said Brazilian miners found it in the 1700s, but the Smithsonian has no record of that, and a curator says it has never been to Portugal. Records say it came from South Africa's Premier Mine around 1910. In 1928, a Ziegfeld Follies performer paid for it with pearls and cash. Harry Winston bought it in 1951, gave it the name Portuguese, and traded it to the Smithsonian for 3,800 carats of small diamonds.
